tml-01-c1.text: L. G. Valiant (1984). A Theory of the Learnable. Communications of the ACM 27(11), 1134-1142.
tml-01-c1.quote: We give a precise methodology for studying this phenomenon from a computational viewpoint.
tml-01-c1.claim: PAC (Probably Approximately Correct) learning, formalized by Valiant in 1984

tml-01-c2.text: Rob Schapire (lecturer), Zeyu Jin (scribe) (2014). COS 511: Theoretical Machine Learning, Lecture #6. Princeton University.
tml-01-c2.claim: Linear classifiers in R^d have VC dimension d+1, and axis-aligned rectangles in R^2 have VC dimension 4

tml-05-c2.text: Mikhail Belkin, Daniel Hsu, Siyuan Ma, Soumik Mandal (2019). Reconciling modern machine learning practice and the bias-variance trade-off. arXiv.
tml-05-c2.quote: This "double descent" curve subsumes the textbook U-shaped bias-variance trade-off curve
tml-05-c2.claim: Belkin, Hsu, Ma, and Mandal (PNAS 2019, Reconciling modern machine-learning practice and the classical bias-variance trade-off) showed empirically and theoretically that the U-curve has a continuation.

tml-03-c2.text: Lenaic Chizat, Edouard Oyallon, Francis Bach (2019). On Lazy Training in Differentiable Programming. arXiv (NeurIPS 2019).
tml-03-c2.quote: we show that this "lazy training" phenomenon is not specific to over-parameterized neural networks, and is due to a choice of scaling, often implicit, that makes the model behave as its linearization around the initialization
tml-03-c2.claim: The NTK regime is also called the lazy training regime (Chizat, Oyallon, Bach 2019).

tml-06-c1.text: Daniel Soudry, Elad Hoffer, Mor Shpigel Nacson, Suriya Gunasekar, Nathan Srebro (2018). The Implicit Bias of Gradient Descent on Separable Data. arXiv (JMLR 2018).
tml-06-c1.quote: We show the predictor converges to the direction of the max-margin (hard margin SVM) solution.
tml-06-c1.claim: For separable linear classification with logistic loss, gradient descent converges in direction to the maximum-margin classifier, the same solution as a hard-margin SVM, even though there is no explicit margin term in the loss (Soudry-Hoffer-Nacson-Gunasekar-Srebro 2018).

tml-05-c3.text: Preetum Nakkiran, Gal Kaplun, Yamini Bansal, Tristan Yang, Boaz Barak, Ilya Sutskever (2019). Deep Double Descent: Where Bigger Models and More Data Hurt. arXiv (ICLR 2020).
tml-05-c3.quote: Moreover, we show that double descent occurs not just as a function of model size, but also as a function of the number of training epochs.
tml-05-c3.claim: Double descent is not just model-wise (varying parameter count).

tml-02-c2.text: Vaishnavh Nagarajan, J. Zico Kolter (2019). Uniform convergence may be unable to explain generalization in deep learning. arXiv (NeurIPS 2019).
tml-02-c2.quote: we then present examples of overparameterized linear classifiers and neural networks trained by gradient descent (GD) where uniform convergence provably cannot
tml-02-c2.claim: Nagarajan and Kolter (NeurIPS 2019, Uniform Convergence May Be Unable to Explain Generalization in Deep Learning) sharpened the point.
